title: STEP import refuses a legal file: a boundary point lies off a twisted B-spline surface

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: effort:high
labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

labels.name: P3
labels.description: Wrong behaviour a user hits, with a workaround; fix now

labels.name: waiting-for-user
labels.description: Waiting for the reporter's answer; closed after 7 days without one

body:
## What the user sees

The import of a user STEP file with a twisted B-spline flank stops with this refusal:

`a boundary point lies off the surface, outside its knot domain`

The file is legal. A different tool that reads STEP through solidcore opens the same file. The file is private and is not attached.

## Where

- The refusal comes from `Fault::Outside` in `crates/app/src/geometry/import/step_nearest.rs:112`.
- The import path is the truck-stepio path.

## Cause, as found

- The surface is a degree-3 B-spline surface with a strong twist.
- The Newton search for the nearest surface point lands on a neighbouring sheet of the surface.
- The rescue grid has 4 samples for each knot span. On this surface the grid is too coarse to find the correct sheet.
- The defect is of the same class as #1602.

## Possible fixes

- Import STEP through solidcore (#917). This is the full fix.
- Or make the rescue search denser, or make it use the trim boundary.

The work decides between these and records the decision.

## Done when

- A STEP fixture that we made, with a strongly twisted degree-3 B-spline face, imports without the refusal. The fixture is not the user's file.
- A boundary point that is off the surface by more than the tolerance still gives the refusal.
- The import does not become slower by a large factor on the current fixtures.

## Effort

The importer makes geometry. Thus the safety floor applies and the effort is `effort:high`.
